title: Turing machine simulation of a halted run
statement: Let $R$ be a number of registers, let $\Lambda$ be a finite label set, let $P$ be a counter program over those registers and labels, let $\ell_0\in\Lambda$ be its start label, and let $x$ be a bit string. If the counter program started in its initial state is halted after $t$ steps, then the machine compiled from $P$ with start label $\ell_0$ computes the output of that run on input $x$ in exactly $t(2t+3)$ steps, with some space usage.
hypotheses_covered: The $t$-step run from the initial state is halted
replaced:
Let $P$ be a counter program over $R$ registers with a finite label set
$\Lambda$ and start label $\ell_0$, let $x$ be a binary input and
$t \in \mathbb{N}$.  Suppose that $t$ steps of $P$ on $x$, started from the
initial state (label $\ell_0$, all registers $0$, nothing read, empty output),
reach a halted state, and let $y$ be its output.  Then the multi-tape Turing
machine compiled from $P$ with start label $\ell_0$, which keeps each register
on its own work tape in unary, computes $y$ on input $x$ in time $t(2t+3)$:
after $t(2t+3)$ steps from its initial configuration on $x$ it is halted with
output $y$.
